title: Bounded Computation of the Encoded Language
statement: Let $C,e\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be Boolean, and let $f$ map finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings. Suppose that for every finite Boolean string $x$, $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$. For every finite Boolean string $h$, the computation started in its counting state with all fourteen registers zero and no result yet halts with the indicator of the following language on $h$: strings encoding a pair $(z,p)$, where $p$ is the binary expansion of a natural number, such that, on decoding $z$ as a pair $(x,b)$, the binary expansion of the natural number represented by $b$ equals $b$, and either $p$ is less than the length of the encoding of $(f(x),b)$ when $\mathrm{mode}$ is true, or the bit of that encoding at index $p$ is true when $\mathrm{mode}$ is false. Throughout the run, every configuration strictly before halting satisfies the machine precondition and has all registers at most $8(2C+3)(|h|+1)^{e+1}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings

replaced:
Let $C,e\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{mode}$ be Boolean, and let $f$ map finite bit
strings to finite bit strings. Suppose $|f(x)|\le C(|x|+1)^e$ for every bit string $x$.

the specified language on $h$; throughout the run, every earlier configuration satisfies
